requirements.statement: Each image object that carries information meets one of the listed conditions.

citations.quote: porteuse d’information](#image-porteuse-d-information), vérifie-t-elle une de ces conditions ?
Image incorporée ou générée par une balise <object>.

routes.statement: The object has a text alternative (aria-labelledby, aria-label or title) and role="img".

citations.quote: La balise `<object>` possède une alternative textuelle et un attribut `role="img"`
Vérifier que l’élément `<object>` est pourvu au moins d’une alternative textuelle parmi les suivantes :

routes.statement: The object is immediately followed by an adjacent link or button to alternative content.

citations.quote: L’élément `<object>` est immédiatement suivi d’un [lien ou bouton adjacent](#lien-ou-bouton-adjacent)
le lien ou bouton doit se situer juste avant ou juste après l’élément auquel il est adjacent

routes.statement: A mechanism lets the user replace the object with alternative content.

citations.quote: Un mécanisme permet à l’utilisateur de remplacer l’élément `<object>` par un contenu alternatif.

exceptions.statement: An image that is the only content of a link has the link's text as its alternative, and the glossary sends that alternative to the Links theme.

citations.quote: lorsque l’image est le seul contenu d’un lien, son alternative est l’intitulé du lien. Dans ce cas, l’alternative de l’image devrait être évaluée avec la thématique « Liens ».

exceptions.statement: An <object> that is the only content of a <button> has the button's text as its alternative, and the glossary sends it to the Forms or Scripts theme.

rationale.text: Test 1.1.6 accepts three conditions, so its one requirement has three routes: a text alternative with role="img", an adjacent link or button to alternative content, or a mechanism to replace the object. The methodology confirms it: the test is validated by an alternative, and otherwise by either of the other two. The first route takes its alternative from aria-labelledby, aria-label or title. The glossary notes on images alone in a link or a <button> (which names <object>) are exceptions: the image's alternative is the link's or the button's text and is evaluated in another theme. axe's object-alt examines only the first route, and only part of it: it looks for aria-label, aria-labelledby or a non-empty title, does not check role="img", and also accepts a presentational role. Its clean result therefore proves nothing, and its fault proves nothing on its own, since the page may use the second or third route, the object may carry no information, or an exception may apply. It looks at every <object> with a data attribute, of any type, but skips hidden objects and objects whose fallback content is rendered, so it does not examine every image object: its scope is partial, and its link is evidence only. No check here resolves the requirement. The second route needs the link's target to be alternative content and the link to be adjacent visually as well as in the code, and the third needs a mechanism to be found and judged; both are judgment. Whether the object carries information is judgment too. So the entry is none. Applicability is judgment, since it depends on which image objects carry information. Needs is empty: the methodology asks for no interaction or assistive technology.

citations.quote: Si au moins une alternative textuelle est trouvée, **le test est validé** ;
